Commentary.Commentary: Right then, that's all from us. The annoying rain has dampened our spirits here but, in the other two warm-up games, the rain has stayed away. Pakistan are taking on Australia in Hyderabad and Sri Lanka are squaring off against Afghanistan in Guwahati. You can switch tabs and follow all the action from those two games. See you there, cheers!

What a bummer! The game has been CALLED OFF! The rain has had the final say in what was the last warm-up game for these two teams. The forecast was always for rain but we hoped that we could squeeze in some overs to constitute a game, but the rain gods showed no mercy. After India's first warm-up game against England was abandoned due to rain, they would have hoped to get on the park here, but it wasn't to be. Rohit Sharma and Co. would not be too unhappy with these two washouts as they have played enough ODIs leading up to the World Cup. On the other hand, the Netherlands would have wanted to test themselves out against India but the rain has played spoilsport.

UPDATE - 3.57 pm IST (10.27 am GMT) - Oh, no! The rain has returned and so have the ground staff with the covers. It is just a drizzle but steady enough for the covers to go back on. Looks like we will have to wait a little longer for play to get underway here in Thiruvananthapuram. The wait continues...

UPDATE - 3.46 pm IST (10.16 am GMT) - The ground getting ready as the groundsmen are out getting the markings right on the pitch. The umpires are yet to decide how many overs to cut down. Let's see what the next update unfolds. Stay tuned with us to know more.

UPDATE - 3.23 pm IST (9.53 am GMT) - Great news! The covers are slowly being peeled off by the ground staff. Let's hope that the weather holds up now, which will allow the ground staff to get the field ready for play. Considering the time lost in this game, we will most likely be getting a shortened game. Stick around for more news.

UPDATE - 3.05 pm IST (9.35 am GMT) - The ground staff have made their way out to the middle and the Super Soppers are at work as well. The positive is that the drainage system at this venue is good but the outfield has taken a beating from the persistent rains. To add to our misery, the radar is showing that it will rain later in the day. We will keep you posted.

UPDATE - 2.50 pm IST (9.20 am GMT) - The rain has stopped and we can see the umpires out on the field to check the playing conditions. The cover is still intact and we can expect another update soon from the umpires. Hopfully we get to have a full 50 over game. Stay tuned.

UPDATE - 2.38 pm IST (9.08 am GMT) - The covers are still on and there are some wet damp patches outside the 30 yard circle to be seen. It does not look good at the moment as the rain is still steady. We still have around 20 minutes before the overs start cutting short. Lets hope the rain passes by before that and we get so see a full match. For now, all that can be done is wait. Stay tuned for further updates.

UPDATE - 2.00 pm IST (8.30 am GMT) - Not much has changed since the last update as it is still drizzling. Considering the amount of rain we have had since morning, it might take at least an hour for the ground staff to get the field to play, once the rain stops. In the meantime, you can switch tabs and follow the action from the other warm-up game between Pakistan and Australia.

UPDATE - 1.30 pm IST (8.00 am GMT) - Aargh! It has been raining since morning in Thiruvananthapuram and it is raining right now as well. The covers are firmly in place and the toss has been delayed for now. The skies are looking ominous but let's hope the weather clears up soon. Stay tuned for further news.

On the other side, we have the Netherlands, a relatively new team with a promising future. They've shown their mettle in the World Cup qualifiers, defeating opponents convincingly. Competing with seasoned cricketing nations is undoubtedly a massive challenge, but the Netherlands has the potential to become a strong cricketing force. These warm-up games are of great importance to them, allowing them to acclimatize to Indian conditions, something they haven't had much exposure to. Every opportunity counts as they prepare for the upcoming battles in the tournament. We all hope for uninterrupted play without rain disruptions. Now, we eagerly await the captains to make their way to the center for the coin toss. Stay tuned, folks, as we embark on what promises to be an exciting encounter between these two teams.

The Indian team enters this warm-up game as the home favorites and carries the hopes of a cricket-crazy nation eager to see them clinch the World Cup after a 12-year hiatus. As a warm-up fixture, team India aims to find their rhythm and fine-tune their skills before the main event. It's a chance for the players to get their touch going and ensure their cricketing rhythm is in sync. Under the prevailing circumstances, India stands out as the top contender for the World Cup title. Virat Kohli and Ravichandran Ashwin are the only two players in the current squad who were part of the 2011 World Cup-winning team. Rohit Sharma, the captain, is eyeing his last World Cup campaign, adding an extra layer of motivation for the Indian side.

Ladies and gentlemen, hello and welcome to this World Cup warm-up game number 9, pitting the home team India against the spirited Netherlands. The match is going to be played at the magnificent Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram. While the weather currently appears fine, there's an 80% chance of rain, and we might even witness a thunderstorm looming on the horizon. This unpredictability adds an extra layer of excitement to today's match. This is the last warm-up game day before the final showdown of World Cup 2023 kicks off and the players and teams will be looking to get in their best shape before the main event.

The stage is set for the next encounter as India takes on the Netherlands in the 9th World Cup Warm-Up match at the Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram. However, the weather gods seem to have different plans, with a 90 percent chance of rain looming over the game. India's recent cricketing journey has been marked by rain interruptions, as six of their last ten matches suffered this fate. Nevertheless, the Indian team appears to be in prime form, benefitting from the home advantage. With only Virat Kohli and Ravichandran Ashwin remaining from the 2011 World Cup-winning squad, it's evident how far India has come. Captain Rohit Sharma is determined to clinch his first ODI World Cup trophy, leading a side that has discovered the perfect balance, featuring the likes of KL Rahul and Shreyas Iyer. The Indian batting lineup radiates strength, and the team aims to capitalize on it. On the other hand, the Netherlands has made significant strides in their cricketing journey. Their participation in this World Cup promises invaluable experience and a morale boost. While they face the formidable Indian side, the Dutch team views this as an opportunity to display their skills and learn from the best. India and the Netherlands share a common wish - to play a full day of uninterrupted cricket, hoping the rain clouds stay away from the Greenfield International Stadium in Thiruvananthapuram. In this clash between cricketing titans and emerging talent, the stage is set for a riveting contest, and fans worldwide await a day of thrilling cricket action, regardless of the weather's unpredictability.
